question: A 72-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of severe, acute, right leg pain for 2 hours. The patient's symptoms started suddenly while he was doing household chores. He has no history of leg pain at rest or with exertion. Yesterday, he returned home after a 6-hour bus ride from his grandson's home. He has hypertension treated with ramipril. He appears uncomfortable. His temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), pulse is 105/min and irregular, and blood pressure is 146/92 mm Hg. The right lower extremity is cool and tender to touch. A photograph of the limb is shown. Femoral pulses are palpable bilaterally; popliteal and pedal pulses are decreased on the right side. Sensation to pinprick and light touch and muscle strength are decreased in the right lower extremity. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the underlying source of this patient's condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "72-year-old man with acute leg pain" -> "sudden onset of symptoms" -> "possible acute limb ischemia" -> "cool and tender right lower extremity" -> "decreased pulses in right leg" -> "indicates vascular compromise" -> "Doppler ultrasonography assesses blood flow" -> "confirms presence of occlusion or thrombosis" -> 85%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man with acute leg pain" -> "recent long bus ride" -> "risk factor for venous thromboembolism" -> "cool and tender right lower extremity" -> "decreased pulses in right leg" -> "suggests arterial occlusion" -> "Doppler ultrasonography evaluates arterial flow" -> "confirms diagnosis of acute limb ischemia" -> 90%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man with acute leg pain" -> "irregular pulse and hypertension" -> "possible cardiac source of embolism" -> "cool and tender right lower extremity" -> "decreased pulses in right leg" -> "Doppler ultrasonography can identify occlusion" -> "helps determine source of ischemia" -> 80%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man with acute leg pain" -> "sudden onset and risk factors" -> "indicates possible embolic event" -> "cool and tender right lower extremity" -> "decreased pulses in right leg" -> "Doppler ultrasonography assesses blood flow" -> "confirms vascular obstruction" -> 90%
analysis: The patient's presentation is consistent with acute limb ischemia, likely due to an embolism or thrombosis, especially given the recent long bus ride which increases the risk of venous thromboembolism. To confirm the underlying source of the condition, Doppler ultrasonography of the legs would be the most appropriate initial test as it can assess blood flow and identify occlusions in the arteries. Echocardiography could help identify a cardiac source of embolism, but it is not the first-line test for acute limb ischemia. Therefore, the best option to confirm the underlying source is Doppler ultrasonography of the legs.
